history.note: Initial enactment of the Capitol Broadcast Attendance Law.

sections.heading: Short Title
sections.text: This Act may be cited as the Capitol Broadcast Attendance Law.

sections.heading: Purpose and National Importance
sections.text: The purpose of this Act is to ensure the uninterrupted distribution of official Capitol information, preserve national unity, reinforce public loyalty to Panem, and maintain information discipline throughout all Districts and territories operating under Capitol authority.

sections.heading: Definitions
sections.text: For the purposes of this Act, 'Official Capitol Broadcast' shall mean any speech, emergency transmission, public information programme, Founder address, Victory broadcast, wartime announcement, ceremonial transmission, or communication authorised by the Capitol Legislature, Ministry of Civic Harmony, or designated state authority. 'Attendance Zone' shall mean any public or designated area in which citizens are required to assemble for broadcast viewing.

sections.heading: Mandatory Attendance Requirements
sections.text: All citizens present within an operational Attendance Zone shall attend and remain present during Official Capitol Broadcasts unless exempted by authorised medical, operational, military, or emergency necessity.

sections.heading: Public Broadcast Assemblies
sections.text: District administrations, educational institutions, workplaces, transportation centres, and industrial facilities may be directed to suspend ordinary operations during designated Official Capitol Broadcasts in order to facilitate mandatory attendance and civic participation.

sections.heading: Standards of Conduct During Broadcasts
sections.text: Citizens attending Official Capitol Broadcasts shall conduct themselves in a respectful, orderly, attentive, and compliant manner. Sleeping, disruptive conduct, unauthorised departure, obstruction of viewing areas, intentional inattentiveness, or acts interpreted as public disrespect toward Capitol authority shall constitute violations under this Act.

sections.heading: Broadcast Equipment Protection
sections.text: No individual shall interfere with, damage, disable, obstruct, tamper with, or unlawfully access any Capitol broadcasting equipment, transmission infrastructure, public display system, communication relay, or authorised state information network.

sections.heading: Attendance Monitoring and Verification
sections.text: Peacekeeper personnel, Civic Compliance Officers, educational administrators, workplace supervisors, and authorised state representatives may conduct attendance verification procedures, identity checks, and behavioural monitoring during Official Capitol Broadcasts.

sections.heading: Unauthorised Information Suppression
sections.text: No citizen or organisation shall distribute information, commentary, visual material, recordings, or public statements intended to undermine, distort, ridicule, contradict, or interfere with Official Capitol Broadcasts.

sections.heading: Educational and Youth Participation
sections.text: All state-approved educational institutions shall ensure student attendance during designated Official Capitol Broadcasts and provide civic instruction concerning the importance of national information unity and obedience to Capitol authority.

sections.heading: Inspection and Enforcement Authority
sections.text: The Peacekeeper Authority, Ministry of Civic Harmony, and Panem State Security shall possess full authority to enforce this Act, conduct investigations, monitor compliance, issue directives, and detain individuals suspected of serious or repeated violations.

sections.heading: Enforcement and Penalties
sections.text: Violations of this Act may result in attendance sanctions, ration restrictions, civic penalties, compulsory ideological instruction, detainment, or prosecution under applicable Capitol and State Security legislation depending upon the severity, intent, and frequency of the offence.

sections.heading: Regulatory Authority

sections.heading: Commencement

sections.heading: Purpose and National Security Objectives
sections.text: The purpose of this Act is to preserve public order, prevent unlawful assembly, reduce risks of organised civil disruption, support Peacekeeper operational authority, and maintain national stability throughout Panem.

sections.heading: Definitions
sections.text: For the purposes of this Act, 'Gathering' shall mean any assembly, congregation, demonstration, meeting, procession, rally, organised event, or collective presence involving multiple individuals within a public or regulated environment. 'Unauthorised Gathering' shall mean any Gathering conducted without approval from the appropriate Capitol, District, or Peacekeeper authority.

sections.heading: Restriction on Unauthorised Gatherings
sections.text: No individual or group shall organise, participate in, promote, facilitate, or remain present within an Unauthorised Gathering within the jurisdiction of Panem.

sections.heading: Assembly Thresholds
sections.text: Any public congregation exceeding the assembly threshold established by Peacekeeper High Command or District Security authorities may be designated an Unauthorised Gathering unless explicit approval has been granted.

sections.heading: Permit and Approval Requirements
sections.text: Applications for public assemblies, ceremonial events, organised meetings, labour gatherings, civic activities, or public processions shall require prior approval from the appropriate Capitol or Peacekeeper authority in accordance with regulations issued under this Act.

sections.heading: Prohibited Conduct
sections.text: No Gathering shall engage in chanting, coordinated messaging, anti-Capitol speech, public disorder, obstruction of transport infrastructure, dissemination of unauthorised information, concealment of participant identities, or conduct deemed threatening to public order or Capitol authority.

sections.heading: Peacekeeper Dispersal Authority
sections.text: Peacekeeper personnel shall possess full authority to disperse, restrict, contain, monitor, isolate, or terminate any Unauthorised Gathering and may issue mandatory compliance orders to all persons present.

sections.heading: Identity Verification and Detention Powers
sections.text: Authorised Peacekeeper personnel and Panem State Security officers may conduct identity verification procedures, temporary detainment operations, searches, surveillance measures, and investigative questioning in relation to suspected violations under this Act.

sections.heading: Restricted Locations
sections.text: Gatherings shall be prohibited within designated security zones, transportation centres, industrial compounds, communication facilities, Peacekeeper installations, state-controlled infrastructure, and such additional areas determined by the Capitol or Peacekeeper High Command.

sections.heading: Mandatory Reporting Obligations
sections.text: Citizens possessing knowledge of planned Unauthorised Gatherings, civil disturbances, unlawful assemblies, or anti-Capitol organisational activity shall report such information to the appropriate authorities without unreasonable delay.

sections.heading: Educational and Workplace Compliance
sections.text: Educational institutions, industrial supervisors, workplace administrators, and District authorities shall maintain internal controls designed to prevent unlawful assembly activity and shall cooperate fully with Peacekeeper enforcement operations.

sections.heading: Emergency Security Measures
sections.text: During periods of civil unrest, insurrection risk, emergency conditions, or elevated State Security threat levels, Peacekeeper High Command may impose temporary assembly prohibitions, movement restrictions, checkpoint operations, or district-wide public congregation bans.

sections.heading: Enforcement and Penalties
sections.text: Violations of this Act may result in dispersal measures, detention, ration restrictions, civic penalties, compulsory ideological instruction, arrest, or prosecution under applicable Capitol and State Security legislation depending upon the severity, intent, and operational impact of the offence.

sections.heading: Regulatory Authority
sections.text: The Peacekeeper Authority, Ministry of Civic Harmony, and Panem State Security may issue supplemental directives, operational regulations, assembly thresholds, permit procedures, and enforcement guidance necessary for the implementation and administration of this Act.

sections.heading: Commencement
sections.text: This Act shall enter into force immediately upon authorisation by the Capitol Legislature.

sections.heading: Mandatory Use of the Official Capitol Calendar

sections.heading: Restriction on Unauthorised Observances

sections.heading: Mandatory Participation in National Observances

sections.heading: Restriction on Unauthorised Symbols and Traditions
sections.text: The display, promotion, or public use of unauthorised ceremonial symbols, prohibited historical references, restricted cultural traditions, or unapproved commemorative materials during public observances shall constitute a violation under this Act.

sections.heading: Educational Compliance Requirements

sections.heading: Inspection and Enforcement Authority

sections.heading: Mandatory Reporting Obligations
sections.text: Citizens, educators, workplace supervisors, administrators, and District officials possessing knowledge of planned or ongoing Unauthorised Observances shall report such information to the appropriate authorities without unreasonable delay.

sections.heading: Emergency Suspension Powers

sections.heading: Enforcement and Penalties

sections.text: No citizen shall engage in Inter-District Travel without possession of valid Travel Authorisation issued by the appropriate Capitol, Peacekeeper, or authorised transit authority.

sections.heading: Travel Justification Requirements

sections.heading: Identity Verification Obligations
sections.text: All individuals undertaking Inter-District Travel shall carry approved identification credentials, biometric verification documentation, transit permits, and any additional operational clearance required by Peacekeeper or State Security authorities.

sections.heading: Checkpoint and Inspection Authority
sections.text: Peacekeeper personnel, transit enforcement officers, and authorised Panem State Security representatives may establish checkpoints, conduct searches, verify documentation, inspect cargo, question travellers, and detain individuals suspected of violating this Act.

sections.heading: Restricted Zones and Controlled Areas
sections.text: The Capitol may designate transportation corridors, rail systems, industrial sectors, military regions, communication infrastructure, and operational security areas as restricted zones requiring elevated travel clearance or prohibiting civilian access entirely.

sections.heading: Prohibited Conduct
sections.text: No individual shall forge, alter, duplicate, conceal, misuse, transfer, or unlawfully obtain Travel Authorisation documentation or otherwise assist unauthorised movement in violation of this Act.

sections.heading: Transport Operator Obligations
sections.text: Rail operators, transit personnel, cargo supervisors, transportation administrators, and authorised transport providers shall verify traveller compliance, maintain movement records, cooperate with inspections, and report suspicious movement activity to the appropriate authorities.

sections.heading: Mandatory Reporting Obligations
sections.text: Citizens possessing knowledge of unauthorised travel activity, forged movement documentation, smuggling operations, checkpoint evasion, or unlawful transit conduct shall report such information to the appropriate authorities without unreasonable delay.

sections.heading: Inspection and Enforcement Authority

sections.heading: Enforcement and Penalties

sections.heading: Restriction on Prohibited Musical Content

sections.heading: Prohibited Themes and Expressions
sections.text: Musical or lyrical content containing anti-Capitol messaging, rebellion advocacy, civil unrest encouragement, unauthorised political expression, restricted historical references, prohibited cultural symbolism, unlawful assembly promotion, or themes deemed damaging to public morale or national stability shall be prohibited.

sections.heading: Restriction on Unauthorised Performances
sections.text: No public musical gathering, performance, recital, concert, broadcast, or organised cultural event shall occur without approval from the Ministry of Civic Harmony or such authorised authority designated under this Act.

sections.heading: Approved Cultural Standards
sections.text: The Ministry of Civic Harmony may establish approved musical standards, patriotic performance programmes, authorised lyrical guidance, ceremonial compositions, and state-sanctioned cultural material intended to reinforce loyalty, unity, and obedience to the Capitol.

sections.heading: Broadcast and Distribution Restrictions
sections.text: No communication network, educational institution, workplace, entertainment venue, transportation system, or broadcasting platform shall transmit or distribute Prohibited Content or facilitate access to unlawful musical material.

sections.heading: Inspection and Confiscation Authority
sections.text: Peacekeeper personnel, Cultural Compliance Officers, and authorised Panem State Security representatives may inspect venues, communications systems, recording devices, public events, educational facilities, and private property where reasonable suspicion exists of violations under this Act.

sections.heading: Educational and Youth Restrictions
sections.text: All educational institutions and youth programmes operating within Panem shall prohibit access to unauthorised musical material and shall provide instruction concerning approved patriotic cultural standards and civic loyalty obligations.

sections.heading: Mandatory Reporting Obligations
sections.text: Citizens possessing knowledge of Prohibited Content, unlawful performances, unauthorised broadcasts, illegal recordings, or anti-Capitol cultural activity shall report such information to the appropriate authorities without unreasonable delay.

sections.heading: Emergency Cultural Suppression Powers

sections.heading: Inspection and Enforcement Authority

sections.heading: Enforcement and Penalties

sections.heading: Regulatory Authority

sections.heading: Short Title
sections.text: This Act may be cited as the Capitol Language Standardisation Act.

sections.heading: Purpose and National Information Objectives
sections.text: The purpose of this Act is to preserve linguistic discipline, regulate public terminology, strengthen cultural unity, suppress destabilising expressions, and ensure the continued authority of approved Capitol communication standards throughout Panem.

sections.heading: Definitions
sections.text: For the purposes of this Act, 'Prohibited Expression' shall mean any phrase, slogan, meme, coded terminology, symbolic wording, unauthorised slang, or cultural reference deemed harmful to public order, national dignity, Capitol authority, or social discipline. 'Authorised Terminology' shall mean officially approved language standards issued by the Ministry of Civic Harmony.

sections.heading: Official Language Authority
sections.text: The Capitol shall possess exclusive authority to establish, approve, regulate, prohibit, or amend authorised public terminology, civic language standards, communication practices, and restricted expressions throughout Panem.

sections.heading: Restriction on Prohibited Expressions
sections.text: No individual or organisation shall publicly distribute, promote, display, repeat, reproduce, transmit, or encourage the use of Prohibited Expressions in any public, educational, commercial, digital, or state-regulated environment.

sections.heading: Prohibited Memetic and Destabilising Content
sections.text: The following categories of expression are prohibited under this Act: destabilising numerical meme references including the '6-7' meme; unauthorised cultural mascot figures including 'Labubus'; and all forms of cognitively degrading or socially disruptive 'brainrot' meme content as determined by the Ministry of Civic Harmony. Such material shall be classified as culturally corrosive and inconsistent with approved Capitol communication standards.

sections.heading: Educational and Workplace Compliance
sections.text: Educational institutions, workplaces, transportation authorities, industrial facilities, and public communication networks shall prohibit the dissemination of Prohibited Expressions and shall maintain compliance with Authorised Terminology standards established under this Act.

sections.heading: Digital and Broadcast Restrictions
sections.text: No communication network, digital platform, broadcast system, entertainment service, or public information environment operating within Panem shall permit the distribution, transmission, storage, or promotion of Prohibited Expressions or unauthorised linguistic content.

sections.heading: Inspection and Enforcement Authority
sections.text: The Ministry of Civic Harmony, Panem State Security, and authorised Peacekeeper personnel may inspect public communications, educational materials, digital platforms, broadcast systems, entertainment venues, and organised events for the purposes of enforcing compliance with this Act.

sections.heading: Mandatory Reporting Obligations
sections.text: Citizens possessing knowledge of prohibited linguistic activity, unlawful distribution of restricted meme content, anti-Capitol terminology, or repeated violations of this Act shall report such information to the appropriate authorities without unreasonable delay.

sections.heading: Emergency Linguistic Suppression Measures
sections.text: During periods of civil unrest, insurrection risk, wartime conditions, or elevated State Security threat levels, the Capitol may impose enhanced censorship controls, expanded communication restrictions, emergency terminology directives, or temporary prohibitions on additional forms of public expression deemed necessary for the preservation of national stability.

sections.heading: Confiscation and Removal Authority
sections.text: Authorised enforcement personnel may remove, confiscate, disable, censor, or destroy materials, broadcasts, digital records, merchandise, publications, or communication systems determined to contain Prohibited Expressions in violation of this Act.

sections.heading: Enforcement and Penalties
sections.text: Violations of this Act may result in civic penalties, detention, ration restrictions, compulsory ideological instruction, communication restrictions, arrest, or prosecution under applicable Capitol and State Security legislation depending upon the severity, intent, and public impact of the offence.

sections.heading: Regulatory Authority
sections.text: The Ministry of Civic Harmony may issue supplemental directives, authorised terminology lists, prohibited expression classifications, censorship procedures, cultural communication standards, and enforcement guidance necessary for the implementation and administration of this Act.

sections.heading: Official Restricted Expressions Registry
sections.text: The Ministry of Civic Harmony shall maintain an Official Restricted Expressions Registry within an authorised Capitol communication environment designated for public compliance reference, including but not limited to officially sanctioned Capitol communication servers and state-operated digital platforms. The Registry shall contain updated classifications of prohibited expressions, restricted terminology, banned meme content, unauthorised symbolic references, prohibited cultural material, and such additional linguistic or communicative restrictions authorised under this Act. All entries published within the Official Restricted Expressions Registry shall possess full legal force and shall be deemed legally binding under the provisions of this Act immediately upon publication. No individual shall remove, alter, conceal, interfere with, vandalise, corrupt, or unlawfully modify any entry, record, classification, directive, or published restriction contained within the Official Restricted Expressions Registry. Any unauthorised interference with the Registry shall constitute a serious offence against Capitol information authority and may result in enhanced State Security investigation, permanent communication restrictions, detainment, arrest, or prosecution under applicable Capitol and State Security legislation.

sections.heading: Commencement
sections.text: This Act shall enter into force immediately upon authorisation by the Capitol Legislature.
